sections.title: SURVEY BASIS
sections.body:
**Archive interval:** Two dry-season image reviews followed by a limited non-intrusive instrument traverse

**Instrumentation:** Orthographic image comparison, differential surface profile, shallow ground-penetrating radar, paired broadband magnetometers, and an off-site regional reference logger

**Study boundary:** A coded upland pattern field containing discontinuous rectangular relief, exposed stone, and saturated margins.

sections.title: OBSERVED VARIANCE
sections.body:
**Surface form:** Repeated right-angle edges and short parallel rises remained visible under different soil-moisture conditions but did not form a complete wall or drainage plan.

**Radar response:** Three shallow planar reflectors followed the strongest surface edges. On the return traverse 22 minutes later, all three appeared 0.31 to 0.47 metres shallower while surface control points and antenna separation remained within survey tolerance. A swapped antenna pair reproduced the changed depth.

**Magnetic response:** Two battery-isolated packages recorded the same three-part broadband pulse sequence immediately before the changed radar return. The sequence was absent from the off-site reference instrument.

**Recovery:** The following-day traverse placed all three reflectors at their original depth. Surface profile, moisture, and control-station elevation did not change detectably.

sections.title: INTERPRETIVE LIMITS
sections.body:
**Ordinary explanations tested:** Historic extraction and frost-sorted ground can explain the static surface pattern. Antenna coupling, calibration drift, surface control error, transient interference, and soil-moisture change were tested during the return and following-day traverses.

**Confirmed exception:** The data show a reversible vertical translation of three subsurface reflectors without corresponding surface displacement or a measured change in propagation velocity. The magnetic sequence is temporally associated but is not established as the cause.

sections.title: DISPOSITION
sections.body:
**Finding:** Reversible translation of shallow planar reflectors, independently reproduced during the event and accompanied by a local three-part magnetic pulse sequence. No physical displacement mechanism was observed.

**Action:** Preserve non-invasive baselines. A repeat traverse requires dual radar systems, independent clocks, continuous surface metrology, and a regional reference package operating before site arrival.

**Field restriction:** Excavation, permanent marking, and unattended instrumentation are not authorized by this record.
